subject: Day 84: lock in the sleep routine
bodyText:
Today's focus
Avi turns three months today, the end of the newborn period and the opening of the sleep-consolidation window. The move now is to lock in a consistent sleep-wake routine while sleep is still cooperative, so the structure is in place before the 4-month regression arrives.

Action items
- Lock in a consistent sleep-wake routine this week. Around three months the consolidation window opens, and a fixed sequence built now is the scaffold that carries you through the 4-month sleep architecture shift. AAP sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/default.aspx
- Optimize the sleep environment before the regression peaks: room-darkening blackout shades, a white-noise machine at 50 dB or less measured at the crib, and a room temperature of 68-72F. AAP getting your baby to sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Getting-Your-Baby-to-Sleep.aspx
- Decide your sleep-training stance as a couple now, whether to train at four months, at six months, or not at all, so you are not improvising a plan in the middle of fragmented nights.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Almost-rolling attempts that do not yet succeed. Motor progression continues on its own timetable regardless of how much you drill it.
- [monitor] Sleep beginning to fragment with more frequent night wakings. Note the date it starts so you can distinguish regression onset from a one-off bad night.
- [call within 24h] Persistent feeding refusal or a new, persistent crying pattern that does not match his baseline.
- [call now] Fever of 100.4F rectal or higher. Under 90 days the same-day workup threshold still holds, and blue lips or labored breathing means call 911!

Enrichment opportunities
- Make the lights-out song the fixed final cue of the bedtime sequence, sung the same way every night, so it becomes a reliable sleep-onset association before the regression. Gerry et al. 2012, infant music classes: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Treat bath time as a language lab, narrating each step in full sentences. Nightly baths over the next 18-plus months add up to enormous cumulative language exposure.
- Hold tummy time at about 90 minutes a day across the day. Many infants now tolerate 15-20 minute bouts with the chest fully off the floor. AAP Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 98-126 (~14-18 weeks): 4-month sleep regression typically begins as sleep architecture matures.
- Day 112-126 (~4 months): 4-month well visit with RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2.
- Day 113-128: expect 24-48h of fussiness and low-grade fever after the 4-month shots.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete

- Pushes up on elbows during tummy time
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Tripod position. Builds toward eventual rolling.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pushes-up-on-elbows/complete

- Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Voluntary grasp emerging. Soon followed by reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-toy-when-placed/complete

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete
